subject: Pilot SLA & budget alignment — latency vs. $/1M token trade-offs
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Turner <laura.turner@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 15:08:00 -0500
Subject: Pilot SLA & budget alignment — latency vs. $/1M token trade-offs

Hi Laura — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before I loop in Procurement.

Call summary (short):
- Primary use case: patient triage chat + summary generation for clinician review (avg. prompt+response ~ 1,200 tokens).
- Expected steady-state Q1 usage: 120M tokens/month (growth to 400M in 6–9 months if pilot succeeds).
- Latency target: 95th percentile < 350ms for short answers; longer summarizes can be 800–1200ms.
- Security needs: VPC private deployment (we'll follow up on certs & SOC evidence separately).

Cost/price items we discussed and where we need quick decisions:
1) Unit econ target: you mentioned wanting to be around $8–12 / 1M tokens during pilot. We can configure a low-latency streaming tier (~p95 200–350ms) that lands roughly at $18–22 / 1M tokens with our default model variants, or a batch-optimized tier that can get to ~$9–12 / 1M at the cost of slightly higher p95 (~450–700ms) depending on batching window and KV cache hit rates.
2) Pilot size options: 1) 3-week functional pilot (50M tokens) to validate quality and routing, 2) 8-week capacity pilot (150–200M tokens) to validate economics under load.
3) SLA choices: we can offer a pilot SLA for uptime and regional failover; for strict p95 latency guarantees we need reserved/dedicated capacity.

Attachments: I’m attaching a short MAP and our pricing accelerator that lays out sample unit costs for different batching/streaming configs.

Proposed immediate asks from BrightHealth:
- Confirm which pilot size you prefer (3-week functional vs 8-week capacity).
- Confirm target $/1M tokens you consider acceptable for pilot evaluation (ballpark is fine).
- Any hard latency SLAs that would require dedicated capacity (e.g., must be p95 < 300ms).

Next steps: if you confirm pilot size + target price band, Ben will produce a concrete pilot SOW and sizing worksheet for Procurement.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call tomorrow if helpful.

—
Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:34:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA & budget alignment — latency vs. $/1M token trade-offs

Hi Ava — appreciate the clear recap. A few answers from our side:

1) Pilot size: leaning to the 8-week capacity pilot. We want to stress economics as well as correctness — we can commit to ~150M tokens for the pilot if the SOW matches.
2) Target price band: we had internal alignment around $10–13 / 1M tokens during pilot evaluation. We understand low-latency streaming could be higher but would need to see the trade-offs.
3) Latency SLA: clinical user experience needs p95 under 400ms for single-turn triage prompts. Anything above 600ms hurts adoption.

Procurement (cc) — I'll need a pilot SOW and an indicative pricing worksheet. Also, please include any language around data handling and incident escalation for the pilot.

Laura Turner
Prod Lead, Clinical AI — BrightHealth
laura.turner@brighthealth.com | +1 (617) 222-3344
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Turner <laura.turner@brighthealth.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 10:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA & budget alignment — latency vs. $/1M token trade-offs

Laura — great, thanks. A few concrete options so Procurement has something to move on quickly:

Option A — Latency-focused (streaming-enabled)- Reserved Dedicated Pool (pilot commit: 150M tokens equivalent)- Expected unit price: $17 / 1M tokens (stream-optimized model variant); p95 ~ 220–350ms in us-east under our pilot load profile- Pros: best UX, predictable p95; Cons: higher unit cost, requires reserved capacity commitment

Option B — Balanced (hybrid routing + smart batching)- Shared hosted with configurable batching and a small dedicated warm pool for spikes- Expected unit price: $11 / 1M tokens with tuned batching windows (50–150ms batching latency add)- Expected p95: 340–500ms depending on cache hit rate and payload sizes- Pros: closer to your $10–13 target; Cons: p95 less predictable at peaks

Option C — Cost-first (batch-heavy)- Large batching windows + aggressive KV caching + quantized model variant- Expected unit price: $8.50–9.50 / 1M tokens but p95 often > 600ms for multi-step summons- Pros: lowest cost; Cons: likely fails clinical UX SLOs

Recommended: Option B as a starting point for the 8-week capacity pilot. We'll instrument end-to-end tracing and surface p95 at token-level so we can correlate quality vs. unit cost.

I’ll attach a pilot SOW draft and a simple cost model with sensitivity to cache hit rates and batch window. We can fast-follow with an addendum if BrightHealth wants to convert to a dedicated pool post-pilot.

Action items:
- Ben: share SOW & cost workbook (today) — attached.
- Laura: confirm procurement contact and any contract constraints (data residency, minimum notice for scale changes).
- Monica: can you own the instrumentation checklist and runbook?

—

Subject: Re: Pilot SLA & budget alignment — latency vs. $/1M token trade-offs

Thanks team — quick instrumentation + ops notes before we finalize the SOW:

1) Measurement plan: we will surface p50/p90/p95 token-latency and per-route unit cost in the Console. For the pilot we'll create two routes: triage-chat (short prompts, stricter p95) and summary (longer prompts, higher latency tolerance).
2) Batching knobs: for Option B we'll start with a 30ms window for short prompts and a 120ms window for summaries; we will run an A/B between 30ms vs 80ms on week 2 to measure impact on unit cost and p95.
3) Fall-back policy: if p95 for triage crosses 420ms for 3 consecutive days we will automatically route to the warm dedicated pool (pre-warmed) to protect UX. That failover is included in the pilot.
4) Pilot acceptance: success criteria = p95 <= 400ms for triage route 90% of the time and average unit cost <= $13 / 1M tokens across pilot duration.

I'll embed the instrumentation checklist and the SLO gating logic in the SOW. If that sounds good I’ll publish the SOW and a runbook link for BrightHealth review.

Monica Patel
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference
